name: Equinix
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Equinix is repositioning from a ~$3B-a-year-capex retail colocation REIT into a $5-7B-a-year AI-capacity builder — the June 2025 'Build Bolder' plan to roughly double capacity by 2029 cut long-term AFFO growth guidance and knocked the stock ~18% in two days, but Q2 2026 delivered the vindication print: revenue $2.625B (+16%) and AFFO/share $11.78 both beat, followed by what management called the largest guidance raise in company history. BACKGROUND: 281 data centers in 70+ metros; ~13% of global colocation (retail-segment leader at ~17% per Synergy); 513,000 interconnections; CEO Adaire Fox-Martin since 2024, with Eaton's former CFO Olivier Leonetti arriving as CFO in March 2026. The capacity engine is the >$15B US xScale JV with CPP Investments and GIC (>1.5 GW across >100 MW campuses) plus the $4B atNorth Nordic acquisition; the power stack includes the colo industry's largest fuel-cell fleet (Bloom, >100 MW across 19+ sites), four advanced-nuclear agreements, and take-or-pay utility structures. The 2024 Hindenburg AFFO-accounting attack ended with an SEC closure (no action) and a $41.5M class-action settlement.
ecosystemRole: We assess Equinix as the procurement standard-setter for multi-tenant AI capacity — how it specifies liquid cooling, on-site generation, and grid deals shapes what vendors must build for the entire colo tier — and as the demand-side counterweight to hyperscaler self-build in this file. Basis: direct-to-chip liquid cooling deployed across 100+ facilities, the >100 MW Bloom fuel-cell fleet (the industry's largest and the template Bloom sells against), ~1.25 GW of advanced-nuclear commitments and LOIs (Oklo, Radiant, Rolls-Royce SMR, Stellaria), and the Central Georgia EMC take-or-pay structure where Equinix funds 100% of grid upgrades — a ratepayer-protection template regulators will point other operators toward. Its constraint is the market's: 0.3% vacancy in Northern Virginia and moratoria in Amsterdam/Singapore make power, not demand, the growth gate.

productsAndServices.name: Retail colocation & interconnection (IBX)
productsAndServices.description: The core franchise: 281 IBX data centers, 513,000 interconnections (surpassed 500k in 2025), the largest carrier-neutral peering ecosystem, and Equinix Fabric software-defined interconnection (Fabric Intelligence launched April 2026; Fabric Geo Zones data-sovereignty controls in May 2026). MRR per cabinet $2,524 (+7%) with quarterly churn guided 2-2.5%.
productsAndServices.positioning: Retail-segment leader (~17% per Synergy; leader in 16 of the top 25 metros); #2 North America behind Digital Realty, #3 APAC behind NTT. Interconnection density is the moat pure capacity players lack.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct enterprise/carrier sales; recurring monthly revenue model (REIT).
targetSegments: AI inference at the edge of ecosystems
productsAndServices.roadmap: Renewal price increases in a landlord-favorable market (CBRE: NA colo rates +6.6-12.5% YoY) carry revenue momentum.

productsAndServices.name: xScale hyperscale program & atNorth
productsAndServices.description: The AI-capacity vehicle: a >$15B US JV (CPP Investments 37.5% / GIC 37.5% / Equinix 25%) building >1.5 GW across >100 MW campuses — nearly tripling the program's capital; >725 MW at full buildout pre-2024 plus the new US wave; Hampton, GA contributed January 2026. atNorth (February 2026, $4B EV with CPP): ~800 MW installed Nordic high-density platform with 1 GW secured power, liquid-cooling-enabled with heat reuse.
productsAndServices.positioning: Keeps hyperscale AI expansion largely off Equinix's balance sheet while competing for the wholesale capacity Digital Realty leads — the answer to 'colo missed the AI training wave.'
productsAndServices.roadmap: 52 major expansion projects across 33 markets underway; ~1 GW of powered land acquired in 2025; capex guided $5.0-7.0B/yr through 2029.

productsAndServices.name: AI-ready infrastructure & liquid cooling
productsAndServices.description: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling supported in 100+ IBX facilities across 45+ metros; 'more than 270 AI-ready data centers' claimed; Distributed AI Hub framework (March 2026); Cisco/NVIDIA Secure AI Factory blueprints deploying across the footprint (June 2026); managed NVIDIA DGX service; AI Solutions Lab in 20 locations.
productsAndServices.positioning: The colo tier's broadest liquid-cooling footprint — but density figures are unpublished; the claim is breadth, not per-rack extremes.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Colocation contracts plus managed AI services.
targetSegments: Enterprise AI inference and private AI
productsAndServices.roadmap: ~60% of the largest Q4 2025 deals were AI-driven; record $1.6B annualized gross bookings (+27%) in 2025.

productsAndServices.name: Energy & firm-power portfolio
productsAndServices.description: The most diversified colo power stack: Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells >100 MW across 19+ US sites (from a 1 MW 2015 pilot; ~75 MW operating); advanced nuclear — Oklo 500 MW (first colo SMR deal), Radiant 20 Kaleidos microreactor preorder, ULC-Energy/Rolls-Royce 250 MWe LOI, Stellaria 500 MWe pre-order; a Dublin hydrogen-generator trial (June 2026); 96% renewable coverage with a 2030 100% goal; the Central Georgia EMC 20-year take-or-pay with Equinix funding all grid upgrades and overruns.
productsAndServices.positioning: The reference customer for behind-the-fence firm power in the colo tier — every vendor in this file's generation segment (Bloom, SMR developers, fuel-cell rivals) sells against the Equinix template.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: PPAs, on-site generation agreements, utility special contracts.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Nuclear commitments deliver 2030s; fuel cells and take-or-pay structures carry the near term.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Equinix has crossed from power consumer to power developer, and its choices function as procurement standards for the colo tier. Basis: the >100 MW Bloom fleet, ~1.25 GW of nuclear commitments/LOIs, the hydrogen trial, and the CGEMC take-or-pay with full grid-upgrade funding — each a template competitors and regulators now reference.

(High confidence) We assess the Build Bolder pivot has been vindicated by results but remains the central risk. Basis: the June 2025 guidance cut (~18% two-day selloff, six target cuts) was followed within 13 months by beats on both lines and the largest guidance raise in company history — yet capex at $5-7B/yr against a ~1.8% dividend yield leaves no room for an AI-demand pause, and only ~20% of sector pipelines convert near-term.

(Moderate confidence) We assess power scarcity is now the growth gate, not demand or capital. Basis: 0.3% vacancy in Northern Virginia, Amsterdam's >70 MW moratorium, Singapore's rationed releases, and a record ~$130B of blocked/delayed US projects in Q1 2026 — the atNorth Nordic acquisition and the firm-power portfolio are both structured around this constraint.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Hindenburg episode is closed but left a residual measurement question. Basis: SEC closure with no action and a $41.5M settlement — but AFFO remains a management-defined metric and the capex-classification issue was never adjudicated on the merits; the derivative suit against named executives persists.

(Low confidence) We assess Equinix's interconnection moat gives it more AI-inference leverage than its ~13% colo share suggests. Basis: 513,000 interconnections and record net adds coinciding with ~60% of large Q4 deals being AI-driven — consistent with the thesis that inference gravitates to ecosystem density, though the causal link is inferred from bookings mix, not disclosed workload data.
